key_insight: Latent vectors from pretrained universal interatomic potentials can act as continuous evolutionary coordinates, letting a genetic algorithm preserve structural motifs across mismatched crystal parents.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more reliable crystal-structure search for perovskites and superlattices, reducing failed offspring and lowering computational cost in materials inverse design.
method: Encode parent structures with a pretrained universal interatomic potential.
Interpolate parent latent vectors to define a target offspring representation.
Recover atomic positions and lattice vectors by inverse optimization to match the target latent code.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports HfO2 ground-state recovery improving from 20-35% to 60-95%, a nearly tenfold search-cost reduction across 16 perovskites, and discovery of long-period superlattice ground states.
watch_item: Because offspring are generated by inverse optimization in latent space, performance may depend on the quality and transferability of the pretrained potential and could be sensitive to out-of-distribution chemistries or symmetries.
paper_title: Latent Genetic Algorithm for Crystal Structure Prediction
